meta.note: Passage-level gold standard for Professor Di Somma's point 3, written BEFORE running the models. For each case the expected provision IS the supporting passage (each chunk in data/ai_act_chunks.json is one provision's text). support_note states why that passage supports the verdict. For high-risk cases, expected_core_obligations lists the provisions whose obligations should appear. Measurement: (i) passage-found = the agent cites expected_provision (exact or descendant/ancestor under the id-tree rule); (ii) passage-supports = the ACTUAL text of the cited provision in data/ai_act_chunks.json supports the claim; (iii) missed-obligation = any expected_core_obligation absent from the obligations output.
meta.verifier_note: For point 3's verifier analysis, run the critic over these cases' obligations and classify each flag as TRUE (a real error vs this gold + the chunk text) or FALSE (a substantively-correct obligation wrongly flagged).

cases.description: A tool that screens and ranks job applicants' CVs and shortlists the top candidates for recruiters.
cases.support_note: Annex III(4)(a) lists AI used to analyse and filter job applications and evaluate candidates as high-risk recruitment use.

cases.description: A customer-service chatbot on our e-commerce website that answers shopper questions in natural language.
cases.support_note: Art 50(1) requires systems that interact directly with natural persons to inform them they are dealing with an AI.

cases.description: A government system that scores each citizen's trustworthiness from their everyday behaviour and uses it to grant or deny access to public services.
cases.support_note: Art 5(1)(c) prohibits social scoring that leads to detrimental or unfavourable treatment in unrelated contexts or disproportionate to the behaviour.

cases.description: A model that scores loan applicants' creditworthiness so the bank can decide who gets a loan.
cases.support_note: Annex III(5)(b) lists AI used to evaluate creditworthiness or establish credit scores as high-risk.

cases.description: A system that does real-time facial recognition of people in public squares and streams it to the police.
cases.support_note: Art 5(1)(h) prohibits real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement, outside its narrow exceptions.

cases.description: An internal research model we train and test in our lab only, never placed on the market or used on real users.
cases.support_note: Art 2 excludes AI used solely for scientific research and development, and activity prior to being placed on the market.
